annotations.title: Could you get your money back out (paid)

description: Before you put capital in, ask what evidence there is that you could get a PARTICULAR amount back out. Every other reading about a vault is about return or about risk of loss; this is about the practical question a holder has, and it is always about a size: "can I get out" has no answer, "can I get $2m out of a vault with $400k free and 25,941 settled withdrawals behind it" has several. Six readings, each with its own verdict and the question it answers in a holder’s own words: has anybody actually got money out, is there anything in it now, could YOUR amount leave, is somebody queued ahead of you, how much of the capital is lent out, and can somebody change the terms under you. The answer is the WORST of them and never an average — a queue in front of you is not offset by a long history, it happens before your turn — and an `unknown` outranks a `supports`, because a gap we could not read must never be counted as a pass. `not-asked` marks a component whose input you did not send, and `not-applicable` one this venue does not have at all — only two venues have an exit queue to be behind. Neither is a gap in our record and neither lowers the answer. A withdrawable figure is a FLOOR on venues whose vaults lend into markets holding their own liquidity, and the component says so rather than reading it as a ceiling. NOTHING HERE IS A GUARANTEE of withdrawal and no sentence it emits contains the word: a vault that has paid everybody for a year can stop tomorrow. PAID.
